title: Layers important to LoRA adaptation varied across tasks
summary: In an intervention study on fine-tuned Qwen2.5-0.5B, the seven layers most important to adaptation had a mean pairwise overlap of 39.5% by the Jaccard measure across four tasks. Only the first three layers appeared in every top-seven list.
ai_technology: Qwen2.5-0.5B; low-rank adaptation; activation path patching
organization: East China Normal University; Brunel University of London

source_review.scope: Qwen2.5-0.5B four-dataset path-patching Methods and Figure 3

evidence.tested: The intervention compares layer-level learned contributions, then ranks the layers separately for the four task datasets.
evidence.unknown: The overlap depends on selected datasets, model, rankings and layer cutoff. It does not establish identical sparsity across architectures.
evidence.ai_role: Path patching intervened on learned LoRA activations to measure each layer’s contribution on four datasets.
